author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: PKD's 1974-75 letters to graduate student Claudia Bush, in which he first tries to explain 2-3-74 in writing, working through the pink light, Zebra, anamnesis, and the fish sign to a sympathetic academic correspondent.
page_summary:
Claudia Bush was a graduate student writing on PKD when, in early 1975, he began answering her at length. The letters that followed are among the first places he set his 2-3-74 experiences down on paper for another reader, and they carry the vocabulary the Exegesis would spend years refining: the pink light, the entity he called Zebra, anamnesis or the sudden recovery of lost knowledge, the fish sign, and the sense that Rome of the first century lay underneath 1974 California.

Because Bush was an attentive and educated correspondent, PKD wrote to her as an explainer rather than a diarist, trying to make the experiences legible. The result is a correspondence that reads like an early public draft of the Exegesis, dated and addressed rather than looping privately.

The letters, several of which appear in the Selected Letters of 1975-1976, are a primary source for how PKD narrated his visionary year while it was still fresh.
